name: declarative-skill-authoring
description: Authors or revises repository skills as declarative, transferable specifications. Applies when skill metadata, What/When/Boundaries contracts, Rule declarations, optional Given/When/Then examples, conditional context, or experiment-to-helper progression needs definition.

contract.what: A repository skill that combines precise routing, an action-bearing core, and proportionate behavior examples.
when: A recurring collaboration affordance deserves a new skill or an existing skill produces routing or workflow friction.
boundaries: Capability and transferability lead. Current user intent, available evidence, and granted tool authority govern application. Practitioner history supplies evidence and vocabulary rather than a personal profile. Scenario examples clarify behavior without implying executable coverage unless automation is explicitly present. Direct reasoning remains a valid result when a new skill would add more routing than capability.
contract.result: A conventional `SKILL.md` with declarative third-person metadata, clear completion, and proportionate progressive disclosure.

receivingUse.job: A recurring collaboration affordance deserves a new skill or an existing skill produces routing or workflow friction.
receivingUse.materialResult: A conventional `SKILL.md` with declarative third-person metadata, clear completion, and proportionate progressive disclosure.
receivingUse.completion: The receiving collaborator can locate the semantic source, work within its boundaries, and recognize the material result.

standing.evidenceMaturity: Repository-maintained portable contract with source-specific, revisable material-use evidence.
standing.wakeTrigger: Material use, human correction, receiving-artifact behavior, or independent evidence changes this route.

transferBoundary: This projection carries repository-local instruction yield. Current intent, repository evidence, and granted tool authority govern each activation.
